newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black empowerment expands into S.African catering.
newsitem.headline: Black empowerment expands into S.African catering.

text.p: Two major black-led South African trade unions have acquired a controlling stake in Capitol Caterers, a Pietermaritzburg-based company operating in KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces.

The National Education, Health and Allied Workers' Union (Nehawu) and the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (Numsa) had taken a 60 percent holding in Capitol for an undisclosed sum, the company said in a statement.
Funded by New Republic Bank Ltd, the deal would allow Capitol to expand nationally and particularly into the substantial Gauteng market, the company said.

"We confidently expect this deal to accelerate our already significant expansion and development, adding marketing muscle and giving us greater strategic positioning in both the public and private sectors of our market," co-founder Giles King said.
Capitol was started five years ago by King and Greg Beattie, who retain the 40 percent balance in the company.

"This is a really exciting example of how established business can develop into the new South Africa, combining black empowerment with proven expertise," Numsa's Mbuyisela Ngwenda said in the statement.
